entities.evidence: The son of Shem named in Genesis 10:22 is identified here as the father of Shelah.
Arpachshad fathers this Shelah, whom the next clause identifies as Eber’s father.
The second clause repeats the preceding son’s name and identifies him as the father of Eber.
Shelah fathers Eber, matching the son of Shelah whose descendants are introduced in Genesis 10:21.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for אַרְפַּכְשַׁד with the root left open. The proposed root ארנ has no support in this occurrence.
draft.evidence: Genesis 10:24 names Arpachshad as Shelah’s father. It gives no derivation for the name.

analysis.evidence: In וְאַרְפַּכְשַׁד יָלַד אֶת שָׁלַח, the object marker אֶת identifies Shelah as the child whom Arpachshad fathered. The next clause repeats the pattern with Shelah as father and Eber as child.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” The personal name אַרְפַּכְשַׁד is the subject of יָלַד, “fathered.”

analysis.evidence: Carried forward: this word and its source tagging were reviewed identically at 68111:1, 68109:1, 68104:1, 66578:5, 66578:9, 66578:13.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: Arpachshad is the subject of יָלַד ‘fathered’. The marked אֶת introduces שָׁלַח ‘Shelah’, the son he fathered. The parallel clause repeats יָלַד אֶת before the name of Shelah’s son.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: After יָלַד אֶת, שָׁלַח names the son Arpachshad fathered. The next clause repeats the name as וְשֶׁלַח and identifies Shelah as Eber’s father.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name in its pausal form, with qamats in the first syllable.
analysis.sense: Shelah, son of Arpachshad and father of Eber.

analysis.evidence: The first clause names Shelah as the son Arpachshad fathered. The second repeats his name in וְשֶׁלַח יָלַד אֶת עֵבֶר, ‘and Shelah fathered Eber’.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וְ ‘and’ prefixes the personal name שֶׁלַח, the subject of יָלַד ‘fathered’.
analysis.sense: Shelah, son of Arpachshad and father of Eber.
